slides.title: Timo, the In-Car AI Social Robot, Launches on Kickstarter
slides.highlight: The launch of Timo, an in-car AI social robot, is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Less can be More: What Aspects of Speech Drive End-of-Turn Detection
slides.highlight: This research identifies that acoustic and prosodic features are more effective than semantic text for end-of-turn detection, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Acoustic and prosodic cues are more effective for end-of-turn detection than adding semantic text signals.
card.key_idea: A trimodal classifier (APT) using a frozen ASR encoder, handcrafted prosody, and MiniLM embeddings, evaluated via controlled ablation of all modality subsets.
card.evaluation: Tested on 5,000 utterances from a proprietary English telephony corpus. A+P achieved best F1 (0.93) and lowest false alarms.
card.limitation: Results are limited to in-domain two-speaker English telephony; text may be more useful in noisy or low-resource language conditions.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE DIALOGUE MANAGEMENT FOR GROUP-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to manage group-robot dialogue, providing uncertainty-aware predictions and more interpretable explanations of robot behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian framework for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It uses a Bayesian neural network to handle uncertainty and a hierarchical classification structure to decompose behavior selection into semantically meaningful stages (e.g., initiative vs. responsive).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian models outperformed deterministic and LLM baselines.

slides.title: Using Semantic Uncertainty to Estimate Transition Relevance in Turn-taking
slides.tldr: ESTIMATING TURN-TAKING OPPORTUNITIES VIA SEMANTIC UNCERTAINTY
slides.highlight: This research uses LLM-derived semantic uncertainty to anticipate Transition Relevance Places in unscripted interaction, contributing to the listener modeling goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: Semantic uncertainty from LLM continuations improves the prediction of within-turn transition relevance places in dialogue.
card.key_idea: The method samples LLM continuations for turn prefixes and measures semantic dispersion via Semantic Nearest Neighbor Entropy (SNNE) to identify local shifts in semantic constraint.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a real-time listener response dataset using F0.5, TNR, and balanced accuracy; outperformed prompt-based, SFT, and predictive-entropy baselines.
card.limitation: The procedure is computationally costly, and the authors leave real-time deployment in dialogue systems for future work.

slides.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS. MACHINE INTERACTION PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research compares human social intuition with machine reasoning in predicting human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Humans significantly outperform VLMs and pose-based models in anticipating human-robot interaction from egocentric video.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking human intuition against lightweight pose models (LSTM, ST-GCN, SkateFormer) and various VLMs using pose-only and full egocentric video inputs to predict interaction intent.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 100 HUI360 test tracks using F1-score, accuracy, precision, and recall. Human annotators outperformed all machine models, especially with full video.
card.limitation: VLMs struggle to reason over simultaneous temporal, spatial, and social cues, often reducing the task to simple approach detection.

slides.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT REASONING FOR SPEAKER RELATIONSHIP INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-free multi-agent reasoning framework to infer speaker relationships from conversations, contributing to the social perception of team states relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A training-free multi-agent reasoning framework for inferring speaker relationships from multimodal spoken conversations.
card.key_idea: Introduces Multi-Role Multi-Agent Debate (assigning agents complementary social perspectives) and Multi-Agent Compete (a pairwise elimination tournament) to resolve ambiguous relational cues without task-specific training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the Seamless Interaction dataset (text, audio, audio+text) against zero-shot and debate baselines. Results show improvements in macro F1 and accuracy.
card.limitation: High inference-time cost due to multiple LLM calls, limited to one benchmark, and imbalanced data for some relationship categories.

slides.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to reconstruct and expand real-world two-speaker conversations, preserving turn-taking, overlaps, and interruptions. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on diarization and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: ConversationalVoice transforms real two-speaker audio into separated, reconstructed, and expanded full-duplex speech training data.
card.key_idea: A three-stage pipeline: separation recovers original tracks; reconstruction resynthesizes clean audio preserving source timing/words; expansion generates new, context-grounded dialogue with explicit interaction planning.
card.evaluation: Automatic metrics (NISQA, DNSMOS, WavLM) and Gemini-based scoring. Results show high speaker similarity, acoustic quality, and dialogue coherence.
card.limitation: Evaluation is entirely automatic; downstream gains in full-duplex model training have not yet been measured.

slides.title: Predictive-Coding-Based Autonomous Regulation of Internally Generated and Externally Coupled Processing in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS REGULATION OF INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL PROCESSING IN HRI
slides.highlight: This research proposes a mechanism using a predictive-coding-inspired variational recurrent neural network to balance internal predictions and external sensory input during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A predictive-coding mechanism for robots to autonomously balance internal predictions and external sensory input during interaction.
card.key_idea: A PV-RNN uses accumulated reconstruction error to switch between high-meta-prior (internal-driven) and low-meta-prior (sensory-driven) regimes, regulating the balance between learned dynamics and sensory accommodation.
card.evaluation: Tested on a Torobo humanoid across three physical interaction tasks. Results showed low-meta-prior regimes reduced reconstruction error, prospective prediction error, and physical interaction conflict.
card.limitation: The regulatory policy and hyperparameters are predefined and calibrated manually rather than learned autonomously from training data.
